front: What is the closest star to Earth besides the Sun?

back: About 13.8 billion years, based on measurements of the cosmic microwave background.
The distance light travels in one year: about 9.46 trillion km (5.88 trillion miles).

front: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
back: Jupiter. Its Great Red Spot storm alone is larger than Earth.
The Moon passes between Earth and the Sun, blocking sunlight from reaching parts of Earth's surface.

front: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?
back: The Milky Way. It contains an estimated 100–400 billion stars.
A region of spacetime where gravity is so strong that nothing — not even light — can escape past the event horizon.

front: What is the Great Red Spot on Jupiter?
back: A giant anticyclonic storm that has persisted for at least 350 years. It is slowly shrinking.

front: How many planets are in our solar system?
back: 8: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. (Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.)

front: What is the Sun primarily made of?
back: About 73% hydrogen and 25% helium. Nuclear fusion converts hydrogen into helium, releasing enormous energy.

front: What is the smallest planet in our solar system?
back: Mercury, with a radius of about 2,440 km.

front: How long does it take Earth to orbit the Sun?
back: 365.25 days — that extra quarter day is why we have a leap year every four years.
An extremely powerful explosion marking the death of a massive star. It can briefly outshine an entire galaxy.

front: What is the International Space Station (ISS)?
back: A habitable satellite in low Earth orbit (~400 km up), continuously crewed since November 2000.
An undetected form of matter making up ~27% of the universe. It does not interact with light but exerts gravitational effects.
